title: $4,120 recoverable — $890 expires in 21 days
narrative: The expiring claim files first, then the batches. Nothing here changes a price or moves a unit — the whole downside of this stage is a marketplace saying no.
status_note: Execute · 0 of 4 stages · expiring claim files first

verification.label: Case outcomes
verification.detail: Approvals post to the Cash lens; denials get one appeal with new evidence, then a write-off entry.

verification.label: Recovery rate by type
verification.detail: Outcomes rewrite the win rates the ledger sorts by. Past 25% denials in a type, the batch path pauses.

verification.label: Window alarms
verification.detail: Any staged claim inside seven days of its deadline escalates rather than expiring quietly.

plan.name: Batch filing via API
plan.meta: 9 claims · one batch per type, one evidence shape each, case IDs captured on acknowledgement

items.name: Dimension-tier batch · 6 claims
items.detail: Filed together with the measured-dimension records and itemised fee lines attached. Batching keeps case volume legible to a reviewer who sees the same argument six times.

items.name: Unreimbursed inventory · 2 claims
items.detail: Both claimed at landed cost from the originating PO rather than at retail — the cost basis history says gets approved.

items.name: Refund without return · 2 orders
items.detail: Filed first in the batch because it has the least window left. Refund events, elapsed return window and the empty inbound-scan search all attached.

plan.name: Portal tasks and document requests
plan.meta: where no API path exists, or the evidence is with someone else

items.name: Walmart shortage · portal task
items.detail: WFS shortage claims file through the seller portal by hand. A task with the assembled pack attached goes to the Controller, dated against the 44-day window.

items.name: Condition photographs · 3PL portal
items.detail: Request to the 3PL for the four damaged units. The claim is assembled and waiting; it files itself the moment the images land.

items.name: Carrier POD and bill of lading
items.detail: Request to the freight broker on PO-4488. Without both documents the shortage claim wins about a fifth of the time, so it does not go early.

plan.name: Cash lens posting
plan.meta: expected recovery scheduled, realised recovery attributed on approval

items.name: Expected recovery on the ladder
items.detail: Placed at the historic decision lag per type — 9 days for dimension claims, 18 for inventory — so the forecast is not optimistic about timing.

items.name: Attribution tile updated
items.detail: Recovered dollars stay attributed to this flow with their claim references, so the period figure is auditable line by line rather than asserted.

items.name: Write-off log posted
items.detail: $84 of sub-floor leakage recorded against the period. Not chased, still counted — the number that argues for fixing the cause.

plan.name: Monitoring
plan.meta: case outcomes, recovery rate by type, discrepancy inflow

items.name: Case outcomes polled daily
items.detail: Every case ID is polled for a decision. An approval posts to the Cash lens; a denial gets one appeal with new evidence and then a write-off entry.

items.name: Recovery rate by type
items.detail: Outcomes update the win rates this ledger sorts by. A type that starts losing gets a lower priority and, past 25% denials, loses the batch path.

items.name: Discrepancy inflow watch
items.detail: Seventeen this month against eleven in May. A fourth consecutive rise opens a 10.1 investigation into why fees are drifting rather than filing another batch.
